prompt: Triage a whole stack trace: pull out its frames and find the deepest one that belongs to your own code. Complete StackTraceNavigator, then run the tests.
explanation: A stack trace is just text with three kinds of line, so filtering on the trimmed prefix "at " is enough to separate the frames from the message and any "Caused by:" header. Frames are printed innermost-first, which is why the FIRST frame matching your own package is the deepest point your code reached -- and usually where the bug lives, not in the framework frames below it. Matching the prefix against the text after "at " (rather than anywhere in the line) keeps a file name or message from producing a false hit.
hints: trace.split("\n", -1) gives the lines; trim each one before testing it with startsWith("at ").
Build frames() first, then write deepestFrameIn on top of it instead of scanning the raw text again.
Compare the prefix against the text AFTER "at " -- frame.substring(3).trim() -- so only the class name can match.
